description: Object to the application of a passed proposal during its timelock window. Writes an objector-signed net.openfederation.governance.objection record into the objector's own repo. The change is held once governanceConfig.objectionThreshold countable objections exist; that threshold defaults to 1. Eligibility is the same community.governance.write permission that gates voting. WARNING: a hold is permanent and there is no automatic re-review — an 'objected' proposal is never reopened, revoted, or applied. At the default threshold of 1 this means any single member with community.governance.write can veto any decision of the community indefinitely, whatever the vote was. Communities that do not want unanimity-by-any-objector must raise governanceConfig.objectionThreshold, which is itself a governed change to the settings record.

reason.description: Rationale published with the objection record.

status.description: Proposal status after the objection; 'objected' when the application is held, otherwise unchanged ('pending-application') because the objection threshold has not been reached.

objectionCount.description: Countable objections standing against this decision, including this one.

objectionThreshold.description: Countable objections required to hold the change (governanceConfig.objectionThreshold; defaults to 1).

objection.description: The objector-signed record, readable through com.atproto.repo.getRecord.

errors.name: InvalidRequest
errors.description: Missing fields, or reason longer than 2000 characters.

errors.name: ProposalNotPending
errors.description: The proposal is not awaiting application, so there is no window to object into.

errors.name: ObjectionWindowClosed
errors.description: The timelock window has elapsed, or the application is already held by an objection.

errors.name: AlreadyObjected
errors.description: You have already objected to this proposal.

errors.name: NotMember
errors.description: Caller is not a member of this community.

errors.name: ObjectionNotRecordable
errors.description: The objector has no repository, so the objection cannot be written as an objector-signed record and is refused rather than held on unverifiable evidence.
